label: West v. Atkins
posture: section 1983 state-actor holding on contract physician
proposition: A private contractor performing a function the State is constitutionally obligated to provide acts under color of state law.

label: Harlow v. Fitzgerald
proposition: Officials are immune unless they violate clearly established rights.

label: Wyatt v. Cole
proposition: Qualified immunity as enunciated in Harlow is not available to private defendants in the circumstances of that case.

label: Richardson v. McKnight
posture: private prison guards; history-and-policy QI test
proposition: Profit-driven private prison guards were not entitled to qualified immunity.

label: Monell v. Department of Social Services
proposition: Local-government liability requires an official policy or custom.

label: Shanks v. Dressel
proposition: The right to non-arbitrary decision-making by officials exercising mandatory duties is clearly established.

label: In re Dwyer
posture: state habeas; HOPE blanket retention condemned
proposition: HOPE's practice of retaining participants for the full parole term regardless of progress was judicially condemned.

label: Lerma v. Amazon.com Services
posture: Rule 12(b)(6); Megan's Law claim dismissed; Fair Chance survived then settled
proposition: The PC § 290.46 claim was dismissed because the report showed ordinary criminal records, not Megan's Law website use. Do not treat the later settlement as a win on the registry theory.

label: Williams (Tameny public-policy hire)
citation: defense construction of Tameny in UPS MTD
proposition: Defense uses Williams to knock the Tameny label on Count II; it does not erase the § 290.46 private right of action.

label: Ashcroft v. Iqbal
proposition: A complaint must plead facts that state a plausible claim.
